statements.impact_statement: The five accepted stackstate-backup-cli v0.10.0 release archives (darwin/amd64, darwin/arm64, linux/amd64, linux/arm64 and windows/amd64) contain binaries from 5feee112a425fcdf3bf92e15b5809cf61f68d612. Source dependency and five-binary symbol/govulncheck inspection show no affected golang.org/x/crypto/openpgp package or call; the source links x/crypto/sha3. Module-level matching reports the parent x/crypto v0.56.0 even though the affected implementation is absent. This is a backup-specific applicability assessment, not a fixed-version claim.
statements.status_notes: Evidence: https://github.com/StackVista/cve-reporter/issues/57 and independent all-five-asset delivery review https://omnigent.tooling.stackstate.io/c/828da530563e5baca8d2c3a4ab6f6fbe. Archive SHA256 identities match GitHub release v0.10.0, published checksums, CDN and scan35083378323. Product versions here are archive content hashes, not OCI manifest digests. Central scanning still uses shared cve-release-artifact identity; these archive PURLs intentionally do not match it. Safe identity repair and consumption verification are required under https://github.com/StackVista/cve-reporter/issues/62 before this proposal can affect that scan. UNKNOWN GO-2026-5932 is present in independent SBOM scans across all five assets. Empty Unix Grype detections are not clean evidence: https://github.com/StackVista/cve-reporter/issues/68.
statements.action_statement: Limit this decision to the five listed archive hashes. Reassess changed archives or an affected OpenPGP import. Human VEX approval is required; this proposal does not grant an exception, change a delivery decision or establish clean closure.
